prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1451; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when the third-party vehicle struck the rear bumper. Claimant reports neck strain and stiffness, no airbag deployment on either vehicle. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says they are handling the matter directly. Claimant describes immediate neck pain and limited rotation to the left. Claimant has not yet seen a physician but plans to book an appointment this week. Explained the claims process and that medical documentation will be needed to evaluate the injury. Provided claim number and adjuster contact details.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report. Officer noted the third-party driver admitted to looking at a phone before impact. Liability appears clear on the third-party side, subject to final review. Insured statement recorded and consistent with the scene photos. Vehicle damage estimate requested from the body shop.

Entry 4: Claimant sent photos of a urgent care visit summary. Diagnosis listed as cervical strain with recommendation for physical therapy and over-the-counter anti-inflammatories. Follow-up with primary care scheduled. Requested itemized medical bills and records from the provider with claimant's signed authorization, which was received the same day.

Entry 5: Physical therapy evaluation received, documenting reduced cervical range of motion and a treatment plan of eight visits over six weeks. Claimant reports pain has improved but is not fully resolved. Medical file flagged for ongoing review. Set diary reminder to request updated therapy notes and discuss settlement range once treatment concludes. Claimant reminded of their right to seek legal advice at any time.
